models_evaluated: Finger fold index (FFI) machine learning computer vision pipeline

links.outcome: Proportion of images and joints unusable by the FFI algorithm because of input quality
links.effect: 78.3% of patient-acquired and 73.5% of HCP-acquired images were suitable to run the ML model; 23.1% of cropped joints were removed after the algorithm ran because of false detection.
links.quote: 23.1% of the cropped joints had to be removed after the running of the FFI algorithm due to false diameter or finger fold detection e.g. due to wrong hand positioning.

unlisted_practices: Patient self-acquired smartphone imaging integrated into a registry app with written photo instructions

screen.reason: The study deploys a smartphone photo function integrated into a real-world patient registry (mySCQM app) to evaluate patient engagement, real-world image quality, and ML-based biomarker performance for tracking arthritis.
